Convert a lag sequential analysis fit to a transition network for tna

Source: R/tna-bridge.R
lsa_to_tna.Rd

lsa_to_tna() converts a lag sequential analysis fit to a transition network for the tna package: a tna network from an lsa fit, or a group_tna from a grouped fit, so that a network found by LSA can be analysed with the network tools of tna. Lag sequential analysis and Transition Network Analysis (TNA) read the same transitions from two angles. LSA tests which transitions are more or less frequent than independence predicts; TNA treats the transition probabilities as a weighted network and studies its structure with centralities, communities, cliques and resampling-based pruning.

The edge weights are chosen by weights: the transition probabilities (the TNA model), the counts, the positive adjusted residuals (the over-representation network) or the lift. With probabilities or counts the network also carries the initial-state probabilities and the sequences, so the resampling functions of tna can be used on it. With residuals or lift it carries neither, because tna would re-estimate probabilities from the sequences; resample with bootstrap_lsa() instead.

Usage

lsa_to_tna(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
lsa_to_tna(x, weights = c("prob", "count", "adj_res", "lift"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
lsa_to_tna(x, weights = c("prob", "count", "adj_res", "lift"), ...)

Arguments

x

An lsa fit from lsa(), or a grouped fit from lsa(..., group = ).

...

Passed between methods.

weights

Edge weights: "prob" (default, transition probabilities), "count" (observed counts), "adj_res" (adjusted residuals, negative values set to 0) or "lift" (observed over expected counts).

Value

A tna object (for an lsa fit) or a group_tna object (one tna per group, for a grouped fit), read with the functions of the tna package.

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and lagdynamics_missing_package when tna is not installed. With weights = "adj_res" or "lift" and a fit that has sequences, a warning of class lagdynamics_tna_no_data notes that the network carries no sequence data.

See also

transition_probabilities() and initial() for the same parameters as tidy tables; lsa().

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement)
net <- lsa_to_tna(fit, weights = "prob")
tna::centralities(net)
